identity.author: Perpetua, Saturus, and the Redactor
identity.edition: Gebhardt, Acta martyrum selecta (1902), Passio SS. Perpetuae et Felicitatis

source_text: Et uenimus prope locum, cuius loci parietes tales erant quasi de luce aedificati; et ante ostium loci illius angeli quattuor introeuntes uestierunt nos stolas candidas. Et introiuimus, et audiuimus uocem unitam dicentem: Agios, agios, agios, sine cessatione. Et uidimus in eodem loco sedentem quasi hominem canum, niueos habentem capillos et uultu iuuenili, cuius pedes non uidimus. Et in dextera et in sinistra eius seniores quattuor, et post illos ceteri seniores conplures. Introiuimus cum admiratione et stetimus ante thronum, et quattuor angeli subleuauerunt nos, et osculati sumus illum, et de manu sua traiecit nobis in faciem. Et ceteri seniores dixerunt nobis: Stemus ad orationem. Et stetimus et pacem fecimus. Et dixerunt nobis seniores: Ite et ludite. Et dixi Perpetuae: Habes quod uis. Et dixit mihi: Deo gratias, ut, quomodo in carne hilaris fui, hilarior sim et hic modo.
english: We came near to the place whose walls were as if built of light, and before the door of that place four angels, as we entered, clothed us in white robes. And we went in, and we heard a united voice saying, "Holy, holy, holy," without ceasing (Isa 6:3; Rev 4:8). And in that same place we saw one seated like an aged man, white-haired, with snow-white hair and a youthful face, whose feet we did not see. And at his right and at his left were four elders, and behind them many other elders.

We entered in wonder and stood before the throne, and the four angels lifted us up, and we kissed him, and from his hand he drew across our faces. And the other elders said to us, "Let us stand for prayer." And we stood and exchanged the peace. And the elders said to us, "Go and play." And I said to Perpetua, "You have what you wish." And she said to me, "Thanks be to God, that as I was joyful in the flesh, I am more joyful here now."
